# Results

## Number and stability of roles

The `{python} COV` covariance structure had the lower information criterion and was retained. Player-level bootstrap stability was high for four and five roles and fell markedly for six or more, where at least one cluster dissolved (@fig-stab, @tbl-stab). Four roles had the highest mean stability (`{python} f3(SC[f"{COV}_K4"]["jaccard_ort"])` vs `{python} f3(SC[f"{COV}_K5"]["jaccard_ort"])` for five roles), a difference larger than the 0.02 margin of the decision rule and than the Monte Carlo error, so `{python} KW` roles were retained; the `{python} KAW`-role solution, which agreed better between periods for new players (adjusted Rand index `{python} f2(SC[f"{COV}_K{KA}"]["yeni_oyuncu_ARI"])` vs `{python} f2(SC[f"{COV}_K{KM}"]["yeni_oyuncu_ARI"])`), is reported as a finer alternative. The information criterion was lowest at six roles and changed little between five and eight, so it did not identify a number of roles on its own. The seven-cluster Ward solution from the thesis was not stable (mean Jaccard `{python} f2(A["thesis_ward7_jaccard_mean"])`, minimum `{python} f2(A["thesis_ward7_jaccard_min"])`). Silhouette coefficients were low for all solutions, so the roles are best read as dense regions of a continuous space rather than sharply separated groups.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-stab
#| tbl-cap: "Stability declines beyond five roles, whereas the information criterion does not identify a clear number of roles (Gaussian mixture models, final variable set; player-level bootstrap)."
rows = [{"Roles": k, "BIC": f"{SC[f'{COV}_K{k}']['BIC']:,.0f}", "Silhouette": SC[f"{COV}_K{k}"]["silhouette"],
         "Mean Jaccard": SC[f"{COV}_K{k}"]["jaccard_ort"], "Minimum Jaccard": SC[f"{COV}_K{k}"]["jaccard_min"],
         "Temporal ARI (new players)": SC[f"{COV}_K{k}"]["yeni_oyuncu_ARI"]} for k in range(4, 9)]
pd.DataFrame(rows).style.hide(axis="index").format(precision=2)
```

Dashed line: 0.75 (stable); dotted line: 0.5 (dissolved).](figures/fig1_stability.png){#fig-stab width=80%}

Adding height left the partition largely unchanged (adjusted Rand index `{python} f2(RF["duyarlilik"][f"paylar+sut+ag+boy_K{KM}"]["nihai_ile_ARI"])`). Variable sets without assist-network information gave less stable solutions and only partly agreed with the final partition (@tbl-robust).

```{python}
#| label: tbl-robust
#| tbl-cap: "Variable sets without assist-network information give less stable partitions (stability with alternative variable sets and agreement with the final partition)."
lab = {"kutu_skoru": "Box-score rates", "kutu_skoru+sut": "Box-score rates + shot profile", "paylar+sut": "Possession shares + shot profile",
       "paylar+sut+ag (nihai)": "Possession shares + shot profile + assist network (final)", "paylar+sut+ag+boy": "Final + height"}
rows = []
for s_ in lab:
    row = {"Variable set": lab[s_], "Variables": RF["duyarlilik"][f"{s_}_K{KM}"]["degisken_N"]}
    for k in (KM, KA):
        d_ = RF["duyarlilik"][f"{s_}_K{k}"]
        row[f"Mean Jaccard ({k})"] = d_["jaccard_ort"]; row[f"Min. Jaccard ({k})"] = d_["jaccard_min"]; row[f"ARI with final ({k})"] = d_["nihai_ile_ARI"]
    rows.append(row)
pd.DataFrame(rows).style.hide(axis="index").format(precision=2)
```

## The roles

The `{python} KW` roles — `{python} ", ".join(ROLE[k].lower() for k in sorted(ROLE, key=int))` — differed mainly in shot location, rebounding and blocking, and assist relationships (@fig-prof). `{python} {4: 'All four', 5: 'All five'}[KM] if stable_roles == KM else str(stable_roles) + ' of the ' + KW` roles were individually stable (Jaccard ≥ 0.75); the least stable was the `{python} ROLE[str(weakest)].lower()` role (`{python} f2(JM[weakest - 1])`). Posterior membership was clear for most player-seasons (`{python} pct(FM["p_max_lt_07"], 1)` had a maximum posterior probability below 0.7). In the `{python} KAW`-role alternative, the wing/forward group split into a perimeter wing role and a stretch-forward role, and the wing role was the least stable (Jaccard `{python} f2(min(FA["jaccard_kume"]))`).

![The roles differ mainly in shot location, rebounding and blocking, and assist relationships. Cells show the mean within-season z-score of selected role variables (the two highest-loading variables of each role by absolute mean) in each role.](figures/fig2_role_profiles.png){#fig-prof width=100%}

```{python}
#| label: tbl-roles
#| tbl-cap: "Ball handlers and rim protectors are mostly guards and centres, whereas the other roles combine positions (player-seasons, stability, height and position shares; example players are those with the most minutes)."
roles = pd.read_csv(f"../data/processed/roles_final_K{KM}.csv")
t = []
for k in sorted(FM["pozisyon"], key=int):
    pos = FM["pozisyon"][k]; tot = sum(pos.values())
    ex = roles[roles["Arketip"] == int(k)].groupby("Player")["MIN"].sum().sort_values(ascending=False).index[:3]
    t.append({"Role": ROLE[k], "Player-seasons": FM["kume_N"][k], "Jaccard": JM[int(k) - 1], "Height (cm)": FM["ortalama_boy"][k],
              "Guard": pct(pos.get("Guard", 0) / tot), "Forward": pct(pos.get("Forward", 0) / tot), "Centre": pct(pos.get("Center", 0) / tot),
              "Examples": "; ".join(p.title() for p in ex)})
pd.DataFrame(t).style.hide(axis="index").format(precision=3, subset=["Jaccard"]).format(precision=1, subset=["Height (cm)"])
```

## Roles and registered positions

Roles were strongly associated with registered position (Cramér's V = `{python} f2(FM["cramers_v"])`, 95% CI `{python} f2(FM["cramers_v_GA95"][0])`–`{python} f2(FM["cramers_v_GA95"][1])`; @tbl-roles). `{python} pct(share("Ball handler", "Guard"))` of ball-handler player-seasons belonged to guards and `{python} pct(share("Rim protector", "Center"))` of rim-protector player-seasons to centres. The wing/forward role was mainly made up of forwards (`{python} pct(share("Wing/forward", "Forward"))`) with a substantial share of guards (`{python} pct(share("Wing/forward", "Guard"))`), and only the interior-big role combined two positions in similar proportions (`{python} pct(share("Interior big", "Center"))` centres, `{python} pct(share("Interior big", "Forward"))` forwards). In the `{python} KAW`-role alternative, the perimeter wing role was `{python} pct(share("Wing", "Guard", FA, ROLEA))` guards and the stretch-forward role `{python} pct(share("Stretch forward", "Forward", FA, ROLEA))` forwards.

## Roles and lineup performance

RAPM was estimated for `{python} MM["rapm_oyuncu_N"]` players (penalty `{python} n(MM["lambda"])`; home advantage `{python} f2(MM["ev_sahibi_avantaji"])` points per 100 possessions). In the 2023–2024 test segments, RAPM explained `{python} pct(MM["test_R2"]["RAPM"], 2)` of the possession-weighted variance in net rating; as expected for segment-level outcomes, absolute values were small for all models, and `{python} pct(MM["testte_egitimde_gorulen_oyuncu_payi"])` of player appearances in test segments were by players seen in training.

With role labels estimated in each season, adding role composition (penalty `{python} n(MM["rol_bilesimi"]["ceza"])`, chosen by cross-validation) increased the test R² by `{python} pp3(MM["rol_bilesimi"]["kazanc"])` percentage points, more than permuted role labels did (@fig-perm; *p* `{python} fp(MM["rol_bilesimi"]["p"])`), and this gain came from role counts (`{python} pp3(DM["sayilar_kazanc"])` percentage points, *p* `{python} fp(DM["sayilar_p"])`). However, the gain did not survive the leakage checks (@tbl-comp). When test-season roles were replaced by roles known from the training period, role counts no longer improved prediction (gain `{python} pp3(LK["onceki_rol"]["sayilar_kazanc"])` percentage points, *p* `{python} fp(LK["onceki_rol"]["sayilar_p"])`), and in the `{python} pct(LK["hepsi_gorulmus"]["test_segment_payi"])` of test segments in which all ten players had been seen in training, the gain was not distinguishable from that of permuted labels (*p* `{python} fp(LK["hepsi_gorulmus"]["sayilar_p"])`). The `{python} KAW`-role solution behaved in the same way (training-period roles: *p* `{python} fp(MA['sizinti_denetimi']['onceki_rol']['sayilar_p'])`), whereas for the thesis's seven-cluster solution a gain remained in the small subset of segments with all players seen (*p* `{python} fp(MT['sizinti_denetimi']['hepsi_gorulmus']['sayilar_p'])`) but not with training-period roles (*p* `{python} fp(MT['sizinti_denetimi']['onceki_rol']['sayilar_p'])`). The apparent role effect therefore reflected, at least in part, information about players new to the league that RAPM could not yet provide.

Pairwise role products added `{python} pp3(DM["ciftler_ek_kazanc"])` percentage points beyond role counts (95% CI `{python} pp3(DM["ciftler_ek_GA95"][0])` to `{python} pp3(DM["ciftler_ek_GA95"][1])`). The test had little power to detect synergy: synergies of 0.25, 0.5 and 1 point per 100 possessions for each co-occurrence of `{python} pair` — a pairing present in `{python} pct(P["cift_test_frekansi"])` of test segments — were detected in `{python} pct(P["guc"]["0.25"])`, `{python} pct(P["guc"]["0.5"])` and `{python} pct(P["guc"]["1.0"])` of simulations, respectively. The absence of detectable synergy is therefore not evidence that synergies are absent.

![With role labels estimated in each season, role composition adds more predictive information than randomly assigned labels; this gain disappears when test-season roles are restricted to information available in training (see @tbl-comp). Histogram: gain in possession-weighted out-of-time R² (2023–2024 segments) when role-composition terms are added to RAPM after role labels have been permuted among player-seasons within season; red line: gain with the observed role labels.](figures/fig3_permutation.png){#fig-perm width=80%}

```{python}
#| label: tbl-comp
#| tbl-cap: "Evidence that role composition adds information beyond RAPM depends on how test-season roles are assigned (out-of-time R² gain over RAPM; same RAPM model, tuned penalty and permutation scheme; pp = percentage points; p values are not adjusted for multiplicity)."
rows = []
for lab_, key in ((f"Final, {KM} roles (main)", f"lineup_model_roles_final_K{KM}"), (f"Final, {KA} roles", f"lineup_model_roles_final_K{KA}"),
                  ("Thesis 7-cluster Ward solution", "lineup_model_thesis_archetypes"),
                  ("Earlier 5-role solution (full covariance)", "lineup_model_K5")):
    m, dd, lk = R[key]["rol_bilesimi"], R[key]["ayristirma"], R[key].get("sizinti_denetimi", {})
    rows.append({"Role solution": lab_, "Total gain (pp)": f"{100 * m['kazanc']:.3f}", "p (total)": fp(m["p"]).replace("= ", ""),
                 "Role counts gain (pp)": f"{100 * dd['sayilar_kazanc']:.3f}", "p (counts)": fp(dd["sayilar_p"]).replace("= ", ""),
                 "Pairs increment (pp, 95% CI)": f"{100 * dd['ciftler_ek_kazanc']:.3f} ({100 * dd['ciftler_ek_GA95'][0]:.3f} to {100 * dd['ciftler_ek_GA95'][1]:.3f})",
                 "p (counts), training-period roles": fp(lk["onceki_rol"]["sayilar_p"]).replace("= ", "") if lk else "—",
                 "p (counts), all players seen": fp(lk["hepsi_gorulmus"]["sayilar_p"]).replace("= ", "") if lk else "—"})
pd.DataFrame(rows).style.hide(axis="index")
```

## Sensitivity analysis: role-combination tests

When all lineup-games were included, the naive procedure indicated a non-random distribution of the thesis archetypes among "significant" combinations (χ²(6) = `{python} f2(F0T["chi2"])`, *p* `{python} fp(F0T["chi2_p_naif"])`), and this was also the case under the permutation test (*p* `{python} fp(F0T["permutasyon"]["chi2_p"])`); `{python} F0T["anlamli_formul"]` combinations were selected, more than expected by chance (`{python} F0T["permutasyon"]["null_anlamli_formul_ort"]`, *p* `{python} fp(F0T["permutasyon"]["anlamli_formul_sayisi_p"])`), and `{python} F0T["bh_fdr_sonrasi_kalan"]` survived false-discovery correction. However, `{python} F0T["anlamli_formul"] - F0T["anlamli_formul_pozitif"]` of the `{python} F0T["anlamli_formul"]` selected combinations had negative net ratings, and unweighted mean net rating was strongly negative (`{python} F0T["NRTG40_ort_agirliksiz"]` per 40 minutes) whereas the minute-weighted mean was close to zero (`{python} F0T["NRTG40_ort_dakika_agirlikli"]`). When lineup-games were required to last at least 2 minutes, the number of significant combinations (`{python} F2T["anlamli_formul"]`) matched the number expected by chance (`{python} F2T["permutasyon"]["null_anlamli_formul_ort"]`, *p* `{python} fp(F2T["permutasyon"]["anlamli_formul_sayisi_p"])`), only `{python} F2T["bh_fdr_sonrasi_kalan"]` survived correction, and the archetype distribution did not differ from that expected (χ²(6) = `{python} f2(F2T["chi2"])`, permutation *p* `{python} fp(F2T["permutasyon"]["chi2_p"])`).
